signals.title: EUR/USD — Sovereign Debt Strain + Positioning Washout
signals.text: EUR/USD trades at 1.1193, slicing through the psychological 1.1200 handle and languishing well below its SMA20 at 1.1464, SMA50 at 1.1530, and SMA200 at 1.1613. Escalating French sovereign debt concerns drive European yield spread divergence as Bund 10Y yields sit at 3.45%, lagging US 10Y at 5.26% by -181bp. CFTC Leveraged Funds hold net short EUR positions of -82,445 contracts (6th percentile, z -1.65), shedding an aggressive -23,640 contracts WoW. Options markets reflect intense downside protection demand with 25d RR at -1.53 put skew, while 1M ATM IV of 6.9% prints a 2.9pt premium over 4.0% HV30. In stark contrast, retail traders sit 88% net long on Retail sentiment data, creating an acute institutional-versus-retail divergence that risks further capitulation. Trade bias: Bearish EUR/USD; debt stress and short momentum dominate. Catalyst: Eurozone Services PMI at 08:00 UTC. Risk: Retail capitulation completes and short-covering triggers a rebound back through 1.1250.
evidence: EUR/USD 25d RR: -1.53 put skew (IV 6.9% vs HV30 4.0%)
EUR/USD retail sentiment: 88% long vs 12% short

signals.title: USD/JPY — Carry Support vs BoJ Verbal Intervention
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 158.01, holding above its SMA20 of 156.26 while running directly into resistance near the SMA50 at 158.02 and SMA200 at 158.48. OIS SOFR at 3.87% versus TONA at 1.23% preserves a decisive +264bp carry advantage favoring the dollar. Asian session headlines confirm Japanese authorities are toughening verbal warnings as spot tests 158.00, keeping traders mindful that 160.00 remains the key level that has historically provoked coordinated MoF intervention. In the options space, 25d RR trades at an extreme -2.36 put skew, demonstrating heavy institutional demand for downside JPY calls against sudden intervention risk despite JPY net short positioning sitting at -16,809 contracts. With VIX at 15.3, broader risk sentiment remains calm and carry flows keep the structural floor intact. Trade bias: Long USD/JPY, carry-supported while holding below intervention thresholds. Catalyst: Japan 10Y JGB Auction at 03:35 UTC. Risk: BoJ or MoF steps in with physical intervention, forcing a rapid liquidation toward the 156.00 zone.
evidence: Fed 4.00% vs BoJ 1.25% — 275bp (OIS SOFR vs TONA +264bp)

signals.title: USD/CAD — Crude War Premium vs Retail Positioning Asymmetry
signals.text: USD/CAD prints at 1.4280, maintaining an intact bullish posture above its rising SMA20 at 1.4019, SMA50 at 1.3960, and SMA200 at 1.3854. WTI crude trades at $90.2 per barrel following wide $9 geopolitical swings tied to Middle East tensions, layering a substantial geopolitical war premium into energy markets. However, the policy differential heavily counters energy support, as Fed SOFR at 3.87% versus BoC CORRA at 2.30% provides a +157bp carry cushion in favor of the US dollar. Leveraged funds expanded CAD net shorts by -23,396 contracts WoW to -72,519 contracts, whereas retail traders hold an extreme contrarian stance at 96% short on Retail sentiment data. This leaves retail exposed to upside continuation as US real yields anchor cross-border capital flows. Trade bias: Bullish USD/CAD; policy divergence and retail short squeeze override oil tailwinds. Catalyst: US ISM Non-Manufacturing PMI at 14:00 UTC. Risk: Crude spikes sharply higher on physical shipping disruptions, compressing USD/CAD toward 1.4150.
evidence: Fed 4.00% vs BoC 2.25% — 175bp (OIS SOFR vs CORRA +157bp)
USD/CAD retail sentiment: 96% short vs 4% long

signals.title: GBP/USD — G10 Rates Divergence vs Cross-Asset Vol Tension
signals.text: GBP/USD holds at 1.3207, trading beneath its key moving-average cluster featuring the SMA20 at 1.3370, SMA200 at 1.3446, and SMA50 at 1.3454. The MOVE index sits at 107.3, marking the 98th percentile of its trailing-year range, while VIX prints at 15.3, located at the 15th percentile of its own annual distribution. This acute divergence highlights rate volatility running elevated as fixed income markets reprice central bank trajectories while equity volatility stays subdued. BoE at 3.75% versus Fed at 4.00% delivers a 25bp nominal policy differential in favor of the dollar, though UK 10Y gilt yields at 5.38% command a +12bp spread over US 10Y at 5.26%. Leveraged funds trimmed GBP short exposure to -5,377 contracts, but persistent UK sovereign fiscal scrutiny continues to cap recovery rallies into moving average resistance. Trade bias: Neutral/bearish GBP/USD; rate volatility and moving average resistance constrain upside. Catalyst: UK S&P Global Services PMI at 08:30 UTC. Risk: US ISM Services prints a major contraction miss, driving dollar yields lower and releasing GBP/USD toward 1.3350.
